title: Humans in Space: Can MLLMs Construct Human-Centric Spatial Understanding via Active Exocentric Exploration?
abstract: arXiv:2610.34149v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at zero-shot reasoning, their spatial capabilities are primarily evaluated through static, passive observation. In complex, human-centric scenes, occlusion often hides crucial geometric evidence, and passive benchmarks force models to guess rather than recognize their own visual uncertainty. To bridge this gap, we introduce SATE-Bench, a novel interactive benchmark comprising 316 real-world scenes and 2,525 multi-turn QA pairs to evaluate visual self-awareness and active exocentric view-exploration. It combines a Passive multi-view control with an Active exploration setting, where models start from a severely occluded view and must iteratively query adjacent viewpoints until they gather enough evidence to fully ``sate'' the question, scored by a step-penalized efficiency reward. tldr: 该论文提出SATE-Bench——一个包含316个真实场景和2,525个多轮问答的交互式基准，用于评估多模态大语言模型的视觉自我意识与主动外中心视角探索能力，并发现现有模型在主动探索中倾向于过早终止探索。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SATE-Bench, an interactive benchmark with 316 real-world scenes and 2,525 multi-turn QA pairs for evaluating MLLMs' visual self-awareness and active exocentric view exploration, revealing that current models terminate exploration prematurely.
